solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 29 down to 19); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who's fired prior to his arrest?

definitions.text: One who's fired prior to his arrest?

parts.words: One who's fired prior to his arrest
parts.note: reads like a sacked employee, but 'fired' means having set fires

explanation.surface: Someone sacked from a job just before being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests losing a job; here it means having started fires.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser commits the crime of setting buildings alight, the deed done before any arrest.

clue.text: A pudding sent up cold?

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue says the pudding's letters are read upwards

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of fruit puree folded into cream

explanation.surface: Was a pudding served chilled, or mocked?
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of crushed fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A distant, unfriendly manner is described as cold or standoffish.

clue.text: Right to come in to rouse support for horse-rider

indicators.note: to come in to says the letter enters the phrase for rouse

parts.note: to stir up is to rouse

explanation.surface: A right-hand rein urges a horse-rider into action.
explanation.definitionFit: The loop hanging from a saddle supports the rider's foot.

clue.text: Noted sinner, after correction, is not staying

indicators.note: after correction says the letters of noted sinner are put right by rearranging

explanation.surface: A notorious sinner, reformed, refuses to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not live in a place is not staying there.

clue.text: Form of winter transport needing second shelf

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Winter travel needing a second rack.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle on runners pulled over snow is a kind of winter transport.

clue.text: Travel by sea perhaps from Cornwall? One mile

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the South West of England, abbreviated SW
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone travelling by sea from Cornwall, a mile out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England, hence SW.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving through the sea under one's own power is one example of travelling by sea.

clue.text: Turn with back of foot

parts.note: the heel is the back part of the foot

explanation.surface: Pivot using the rear of your foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin round, as a flock of birds does, is a synonym for turn.

clue.text: Make-up with which mother covers a lasting mark

indicators.note: covers says the letters for mother go round the following pieces

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a scar is a permanent mark on the skin

explanation.surface: Mum uses cosmetics to hide a scar.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmetic applied to darken eyelashes is a type of make-up.

clue.text: Old train's position, say

parts.note: to orient something is to position it
to express is to say or put into words

explanation.surface: A question about where an old train stands.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous luxury railway service between Paris and Istanbul began in 1883, so it is an old train.

clue.text: Items of headgear for lying in?

definitions.text: Items of headgear for lying in?

parts.words: Items of headgear for lying in
parts.note: in rhyming slang a 'pork pie' is a lie, so a hat of that name is jokingly worn for telling fibs

explanation.surface: Hats you might wear in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying in' suggests a lie-in in bed; in Cockney rhyming slang pork pies (porkies) are lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-crowned felt hats shaped like the savoury pastry are items of headgear.

clue.text: Not against an Established Church's power

parts.note: being not against something is being for it
CE is the Church of England, England's established church

explanation.surface: A claim about the authority of a state church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Force and power are synonyms, both meaning strength or might.

clue.text: Primate received, at first, poorly in Indian state

indicators.note: in says the letters are placed inside the state's name

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of received is used

parts.note: poorly means ill

explanation.surface: Someone who fell ill while travelling in India was received by a primate.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ape is a member of the order of mammals that includes monkeys and humans.

clue.text: A New Hope is she

definitions.note: a girl's name stands for a female, as 'she' does

indicators.note: new says the letters of hope is are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Reads like the Star Wars film title A New Hope, said to be female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A New Hope' looks like a title; 'New' is the anagram signal and 'A' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name is an example of a person who could be called she.

clue.text: Broadcast exotic arts etc

indicators.note: exotic says the letters of arts etc are given an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A programme airing foreign arts and other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' is a verb, to strew seeds widely.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to sow it widely by hand, the same as strewing it about.

clue.text: Ancient city strikes back with part-time soldiers

indicators.note: back says the word for strikes is read in reverse

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or strikes
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An ancient city hits back with a reserve army.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is the UK's part-time volunteer military reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The warrior state of the Peloponnese was a major city of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Turning up in mail: a German's ceremonial robes

indicators.note: Turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Royal robes arriving in a German's post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' in a down clue says the letters read upward; 'in' signals they are hidden in 'mail: a German's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal insignia and dress worn on state occasions are ceremonial robes.

clue.text: After rising, comes to English judge

indicators.note: rising in a down clue says the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: meets, as in comes to a total, means comes to

explanation.surface: After standing up, someone approaches an English judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to judge or consider, as in 'I esteem it an honour'.

clue.text: Ask anew for revival — complies?

indicators.note: for revival says the letters of ask anew are brought back to life in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asked again to come round finally does so.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: whoever is asked again to revive and complies comes round; the blogger found this &lit tenuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Complying with a request to revive means rousing from sleep, coming back to consciousness.

clue.text: A right reverend on an island off the Scottish coast

parts.note: RR abbreviates Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island in the Firth of Clyde lies off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Ancient king hated garish displays

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old monarch disliked showy exhibitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth-century monarch of England bore this name, so he is an ancient ruler.

clue.text: Perilous run: one very high place!

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
one is the Roman numeral I
the sky is a very high place

explanation.surface: A dangerous dash up to a lofty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous is full of danger, a synonym of perilous.

clue.text: Hunter battles to alter and completely reverse positions

indicators.note: to alter says the letters of hunter battles are changed round

explanation.surface: A hunter fights battles to change things and flip the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to swap one's weaker position for the stronger one an opponent held.

clue.text: Weakling managed support at the very end

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: at the very end picks only the closing letter of support

explanation.surface: A feeble person managed to give backing at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest, weakest animal of a litter is known by this word, extended to any weak person.

clue.text: Eastern girl: a railway agent

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl

explanation.surface: An eastern girl works as an agent for a railway company.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission is a representative or agent of whoever sent them.
